title: Hinton asks about John Hammond; Hammond arrives in Kansas City
summary: Jones says Basie got letters from Charlie Barnet and John Hammond, and Hammond arrived at the black hotel in Kansas City in 1936.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Jo, you must do that. We must work towards that. There's one thing, Jo, and I ask you this in all sincerity and you can do whichever way you like. At this particular time I'd like to ask you, if you feel like it, to speak about a man that I know and I'm sure you know, that I feel and I'm sure you feel that has made the most tremendous contribution to jazz and to the promotion of jazz.

I know you know him much better and much longer than I. I just have to ask you to say whatever you would about Mr. John Hammond. Walk around or do anything you want, but I want this like Jo Jones wants to say it.

I wouldn't go into infancy years. John Hammond; my name is Jonathan, so is his. You must remember he's coming through a period with another fellow, name of Charlie Barnet. I remember Basie getting a letter from Charlie Barnet and from John Hammond at the same time. I read both of the letters and I said, "You read the one; answer John's." Because Buck Clayton had just come back from China and he was in California. He was on his way to join us. We had no job for Buck, because Buck came in to Kansas City and he played the Movie Chateau and he played the piano till Basie got there, till 1 o'clock and then he picked up the trumpet. (Answer: Charlie.) He said, "No, we answer John's letter." So Mr. Hammond came in to Kansas City and came to the Booker T. Hotel and I was sitting up playing my vibraphones with Dick Wilson with a towel wrapped around, like a bikini, and he came in this hotel and it was a shock to see a white man come into a white hotel -
A white man come into a black hotel?
A black hotel, in Kansas City? Impossible. He looked like a hayseed; he come up there with his crew cut, you looked like a wheat field. He spoke to me; he said,
